content.markdown:
# The Complete Guide to Design Systems & Prototyping with Figma

A design system is the single source of truth for a product's visual language. It ensures consistency across screens, accelerates design, and bridges the gap between designers and developers.

## What Is a Design System?

A design system is more than a UI kit. It includes:

- **Design Tokens**: Colors, spacing, typography values
- **Component Library**: Reusable UI elements
- **Patterns**: Common interaction patterns
- **Documentation**: Usage guidelines and principles
- **Brand Guidelines**: Voice, tone, and visual identity

## Design Tokens

Design tokens are the atomic values of your visual language.

### Color System

```
Primary Colors:
  primary-50:  #EBF5FF  (lightest)
  primary-100: #D6EBFF
  primary-200: #ADd7FF
  primary-300: #85C3FF
  primary-400: #5CAFFF
  primary-500: #339BFF  (base)
  primary-600: #297CC9
  primary-700: #1F5D96
  primary-800: #143E64
  primary-900: #0A1F32  (darkest)

Semantic Colors:
  success:  #22C55E
  warning:  #F59E0B
  error:    #EF4444
  info:     #3B82F6

Neutral Colors:
  gray-50:  #F9FAFB
  gray-100: #F3F4F6
  gray-500: #6B7280
  gray-900: #111827
```

### Typography Scale

```
Font Families:
  heading: 'Inter', sans-serif
  body: 'Inter', sans-serif
  mono: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace

Type Scale:
  display-lg:  48px / 56px / -0.02em / Bold
  display-sm:  36px / 44px / -0.02em / Bold
  heading-1:   30px / 38px / -0.01em / Semibold
  heading-2:   24px / 32px / -0.01em / Semibold
  heading-3:   20px / 28px / 0 / Semibold
  body-lg:     18px / 28px / 0 / Regular
  body-md:     16px / 24px / 0 / Regular
  body-sm:     14px / 20px / 0 / Regular
  caption:     12px / 16px / 0.01em / Regular
```

### Spacing System

```
Base unit: 4px

Spacing Scale:
  space-1:  4px
  space-2:  8px
  space-3:  12px
  space-4:  16px
  space-5:  20px
  space-6:  24px
  space-8:  32px
  space-10: 40px
  space-12: 48px
  space-16: 64px
  space-20: 80px

Layout:
  container-sm: 640px
  container-md: 768px
  container-lg: 1024px
  container-xl: 1280px
```

### Elevation & Shadows

```
Elevation System:
  shadow-sm:  0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)
  shadow-md:  0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)
  shadow-lg:  0 10px 15px -3px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)
  shadow-xl:  0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)

Border Radius:
  radius-sm: 4px
  radius-md: 8px
  radius-lg: 12px
  radius-xl: 16px
  radius-full: 9999px
```

## Building Components in Figma

### Component Architecture

```
Atoms (smallest elements):
  → Icon
  → Badge
  → Avatar
  → Tag

Molecules (combinations):
  → Button (icon + text)
  → Input Field (label + input + helper text)
  → Card (image + text + actions)
  → List Item (avatar + text + action)

Organisms (sections):
  → Navigation Bar
  → Hero Section
  → Data Table
  → Form

Templates (page layouts):
  → Dashboard Layout
  → Settings Page
  → List/Detail View
```

### Auto Layout Best Practices

```
1. Use auto layout for EVERYTHING
   - Enables responsive behavior
   - Components resize correctly
   - Consistent spacing

2. Padding & Gap Settings:
   - Buttons: 12px vertical, 24px horizontal, 8px gap
   - Cards: 16px-24px padding, 12px-16px gap
   - List items: 12px vertical, 16px horizontal
   - Sections: 24px-48px padding, 16px-24px gap

3. Fill vs Hug vs Fixed:
   - Fill: Element stretches to parent width
   - Hug: Element wraps its content
   - Fixed: Element has a set size

4. Nesting Strategy:
   - Horizontal → Vertical → Horizontal
   - Each level handles one direction
```

### Component Variants

```
Button Component Variants:
  Property: Type
    Values: Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Danger
  
  Property: Size
    Values: Small (32px), Medium (40px), Large (48px)
  
  Property: State
    Values: Default, Hover, Active, Disabled, Loading
  
  Property: Icon Position
    Values: None, Left, Right, Icon Only

Total combinations: 4 × 3 × 5 × 4 = 240 states
(Figma handles this with variant properties)
```

### Interactive Components

```
Interaction Types:
  → On Click: Navigate, Change variant
  → On Hover: Show tooltip, Change state
  → On Drag: Swipe actions, Reorder
  → While Pressing: Scale down effect
  → After Delay: Auto-advance, Toast dismiss

Smart Animate:
  - Figma interpolates between variant states
  - Match layer names between variants
  - Control easing and duration
  - Create micro-interactions without code
```

## Prototyping Flows

### User Flow Documentation

```
Onboarding Flow:
  1. Splash Screen
     → Auto-advance (2s)
  2. Welcome Screen
     → "Get Started" button
  3. Feature Carousel (3 slides)
     → Swipe or tap dots
  4. Create Account
     → Form validation states
  5. Profile Setup
     → Avatar upload, preferences
  6. Dashboard
     → First-time empty state

Prototype Settings:
  Device: iPhone 15 Pro
  Background: #000000
  Overflow: Vertical scrolling
  Transition: Smart animate, 300ms, ease-in-out
```

### Prototype Interactions

```
Navigation Patterns:
  → Bottom tabs: Instant transition
  → Push navigation: Slide left (300ms)
  → Modal: Slide up (400ms)
  → Back: Slide right (250ms)
  → Overlay: Fade in (200ms)

Micro-interactions:
  → Button press: Scale to 0.95 (100ms)
  → Toggle switch: Smart animate (200ms)
  → Pull to refresh: Custom spring animation
  → Skeleton loading: Shimmer effect
```

## Developer Handoff

### Design Specs in Figma

```
What developers need:
  1. Spacing values (padding, margin, gap)
  2. Color values (hex, rgba)
  3. Font properties (family, size, weight, line-height)
  4. Border radius and shadows
  5. Component states (hover, active, disabled)
  6. Responsive behavior (breakpoints)
  7. Animation specs (duration, easing, properties)

Figma Dev Mode:
  - Inspect panel shows CSS/SwiftUI/Compose code
  - Redlines appear automatically
  - Assets exportable in multiple formats
  - Variables map to design tokens
```

### Organizing for Handoff

```
File Structure:
  📁 Design System
    📄 Tokens (colors, typography, spacing)
    📄 Components (all component variants)
    📄 Icons (icon library)
    📄 Patterns (common patterns)
  
  📁 Product - Feature Name
    📄 Flows (user flow diagrams)
    📄 Screens (all screens and states)
    📄 Prototype (interactive prototype)
    📄 Specs (edge cases, annotations)

Naming Convention:
  Components: PascalCase (ButtonPrimary)
  Variants: camelCase properties (size=medium)
  Layers: Descriptive names (headerTitle, navBar)
  Pages: Feature / Section names
```

### Design Tokens to Code

```css
/* Generated from Figma design tokens */
:root {
  /* Colors */
  --color-primary-500: #339BFF;
  --color-gray-900: #111827;
  --color-success: #22C55E;
  --color-error: #EF4444;

  /* Typography */
  --font-heading: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  --text-body-md: 16px/24px var(--font-heading);

  /* Spacing */
  --space-4: 16px;
  --space-6: 24px;

  /* Shadows */
  --shadow-md: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);

  /* Radius */
  --radius-md: 8px;
}
```

## Design System Governance

### Contribution Process

```
1. Identify need for new component
2. Research existing patterns
3. Design component with all states
4. Review with design team
5. Build component in code
6. Document usage guidelines
7. Publish to design system
```

### Versioning

```
Semantic versioning for design systems:
  Major (2.0.0): Breaking visual changes
  Minor (1.1.0): New components added
  Patch (1.0.1): Bug fixes, small tweaks

Changelog:
  v1.2.0 - Added DatePicker component
  v1.1.1 - Fixed Button hover state color
  v1.1.0 - Added Toast notification component
```

## Best Practices

1. Start with tokens, not components
2. Design for all states (empty, loading, error, success)
3. Use auto layout everywhere
4. Name layers consistently
5. Document usage guidelines for each component
6. Test prototypes with real users
7. Keep design system and code in sync
8. Review and iterate regularly

## Conclusion

A well-built design system saves countless hours and ensures a consistent, polished product experience.

**Key Takeaways:**
1. Design tokens are the foundation of your system
2. Build components from atoms to organisms
3. Use Figma variants for all component states
4. Prototype interactions for stakeholder buy-in
5. Optimize handoff with dev mode and clear specs
6. Govern and version your design system

Design systematically!
